serialFormats.description: Rheem/Ruud HVAC (current style): 1 plant letter + WW (week) + YY (year) + 5-digit sequence, 10 characters total (e.g. W3520xxxxx = week 35 of 2020).

map.N: Fort Smith, AR (per building-center/pickhvac plant list)

sources: Building Intelligence Center — Rheem HVAC age (https://www.building-center.org/rheem-hvac-age/): Style 1 = letter + 9 digits; first two digits after the letter = week, next two = year
PickHVAC — Rheem HVAC age / serial number decoding (https://www.pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/rheem/): M2215… = 22nd week of 2015; factory letter F, M, G, W or N
hvacchecker.com Rheem HVAC age: 10 characters = 1 factory letter, 4 date digits (WWYY), 5 sequence digits; W3520 = week 35 of 2020
Ruud HVAC age (https://www.building-center.org/ruud-hvac-age/): Ruud uses the same styles
notes: Week/year prefixes in the examples come from the cited decoders (W3520, M2215, 42/17); the 5-digit sequence portions are illustrative — the sequence does not affect the date.

Two-digit year with pivot 70: 95–99 → 1995–1999, 00–69 → 2000–2069. Serials in this style are common from the late 1990s on; a plate with an R-22 charge or a mid-1990s compressor date stamp with a yy of 95–99 is consistent with 199x.
Plant letter W appears on most current units; its plant is not documented in the cited sources (not mapped — do not guess).

Rheem's own page rheem.com/rheem_model_serial_numbers/ exists but its text could not be read in this session, so confidence stays 'medium' (two independent secondary decoders agree) rather than 'high'.
Ruud-branded units use the same serial styles (building-center Ruud page).

One decoder (hvacagelookup.com) claims YYWW order ('F2317 = week 17 of 2023'); the three cited sources and W3520-style serials (a year pair > 53 is impossible as a week) support WWYY. If both digit pairs are <= 53 (e.g. F2317: week 23 of 2017 vs week 17 of 2023), confirm the year from the compressor date code or the refrigerant on the plate.

serialFormats.description: Rheem/Ruud HVAC older style: four-letter prefix (e.g. RHLN), space, plant letter F/M/G/N (or W), then WW (week) YY (year) and a sequence (e.g. RHLN G0304567 = week 3 of 2004). The regex also tolerates a 2–6 character alphanumeric prefix.
sources: PickHVAC — Rheem HVAC age: 'the middle letter of the serial number is the factory code (F, M, G, W or N); week = 1st & 2nd numbers following it, year = 3rd & 4th' and 'Style 2: begins with 4 letters followed by a space and then a letter F, M, G or N, followed by 4 numbers (1st and 2nd = week, 3rd and 4th = year)'; example RHLN G0304567 = week 3 of 2004
Building Intelligence Center — Rheem HVAC age: plant letters M = Montgomery AL, N = Fort Smith AR, F = Oxnard CA, G = Eagan MN
notes: LOW CONFIDENCE: the position/length of the characters preceding the plant letter could not be confirmed from a dated nameplate in this session; the regex tolerates 2–6 leading characters. The first two examples are synthetic (built from the published rule); the third ('RHLN G0304567' = week 3 of 2004) is PickHVAC's Rheem Style 2 worked example. eraEnd 2005 is not sourced.

The rule itself (plant letter, then WW, then YY) is the same as the current style; the era filter (≤ 2005) is what separates this from 'rheem-hvac-letter-wwyy'. If both match, confirm the year from the compressor date code and the refrigerant on the plate (R-22 on pre-2010 units).
Oxnard CA and Eagan MN were closed long ago, so plant letters F and G on an HVAC plate point to an older unit.

serialFormats.description: Rheem/Ruud/Richmond WATER HEATER 10-digit style: MM YY P 12345 (month, 2-digit year, plant letter, sequence), optionally prefixed R / RN / RNG / RHNG. Included so a tech reading a Rheem plate in a mechanical room is not misled — not an HVAC style.
sources: Rheem — How to locate and read your Rheem water heating serial numbers (https://www.rheem.com/how-to-locate-and-read-your-rheem-water-heating-serial-numbers/): current 10-digit code MMYYP12345, P = plant code
Building Intelligence Center — Rheem water heater age (https://www.building-center.org/rheem-water-heater-age/): Style 1 example 'R 0884B10488', month = 1st & 2nd digits, year = 3rd & 4th
notes: Examples: 'R 0884B10488' (building-center, Aug 1984) and '1209D01234' (Rheem's own worked example: December 2009, plant line code D, consecutive number 01234) are sourced; the third is a synthetic test of the published MMYYP rule.
Water heaters only. HVAC serials start with a single letter followed by 9 digits (see rheem-hvac-letter-wwyy).

serialFormats.description: Rheem WATER HEATER style 2: RHLN (or R/RN/RNG) prefix + MM YY + 6-digit sequence (e.g. RHLN 0106534307 = January 2006). Month vs week reading of the four digits is disputed between sources — year is unaffected.
sources: Building Intelligence Center — Rheem water heater age: Style 2 example 'RHLN0106534307' — 'the second and third characters represent the month and the fourth and fifth the year … made in January of 2006' (MMYY)
Rheem — How to locate and read your Rheem water heating serial numbers: all Rheem water heating labels use MM YY P ##### (month first)
InspectAPedia Rheem water heater serial decoding lists the prefixed style as 'ABCD MM YY 2345' (month/year)
fastwaterheater.com water heater model/serial lookup guide reads the four digits after an RHLN prefix as WWYY (RHLN0820 = week 8 of 2020) — dissenting reading
notes: UNVERIFIED: building-center and Rheem read the four digits after the prefix as MMYY; fastwaterheater reads them as WWYY — month vs week is unresolved, the year is unaffected either way. Confidence is 'low' until a Rheem water-heater serial with a first pair > 12 (impossible as a month) is seen.
Water heaters only; second example's sequence digits are illustrative.

Overlap: an RHLN serial also satisfies rheem-hvac-prefixed-plant-wwyy (its trailing N reads as a plant letter); both readings give the same year, and that format's era (<= 2005) drops later units anyway.

serialFormats.description: AAON: serial starts with the four-digit year and two-digit month of manufacture, followed by letters and a sequence (e.g. 200108AKG26241 = August 2001).
sources: Building Intelligence Center — AAON HVAC age (https://www.building-center.org/aaon-hvac-age/): Style 1 example 200108AKG26241, year = 1st–4th digits, month = 5th–6th digits
AAON — What is my AAON product model? (https://www.aaon.com/resources/what-is-my-aaon-product-model): provide the serial to an AAON rep for full unit data
notes: Only the first example is a sourced serial; the other two are synthetic tests of the year-first rule (one secondary decoder plus builder field recollection — hence 'low'). Confirm with AAON factory technical support ((918) 382-6450) or the unit's IOM, which is normally shipped in the control compartment with the order-specific drawings.
The four-digit year makes this unambiguous; the decoder's month sanity check (01–12) rejects strings that merely start with four digits.
AAONAIRE-branded units use the same style (building-center AAONAIRE page).
Pre-2001 AAON units use two other styles (year-first two digits + month letter, or four letters + YYMM) — see aaon-yy-monthletter and aaon-letters-yymm.

controls.name: Rheem Renaissance Rooftop Unit Controller (RTU-C) with PlusOne Diagnostics / ClearControl
controls.description: Factory-mounted solid-state microprocessor rooftop unit controller on RKNL-C/RLNL-C and later Renaissance packaged units. Provides staging, economizer integration, diagnostics with alphanumeric fault codes on the local display and via ClearControl (DDL) / Modbus. The gas-heat IFC reports to the RTU-C over Modbus. Coverage is partial: the manufacturer's 'RTU-C Alarm Table and Diagnostic Guide' (92-103249-01 Rev.03 p.60 / Rev.05 p.66) exists but its rows could not be read through search summaries; only alarms whose behaviour is described in prose elsewhere in the same documents (or in the spec sheets) are transcribed here, using the alarm's functional name rather than its A-number. A15 is the only alphanumeric code seen, and only from a third-party thread. Alarm code numbering (A1…A15+) on the LCD should be transcribed from the alarm table when the PDF can be read; until then the A-number for each alarm above is unknown. Current Renaissance units (RGEC/RGED/RACC/RHPC, 2018+) ship with the non-communicating 'CoreCommand' control — a dual 7-segment LED display with fault codes and fault history, optional phase monitor; the TEST button defeats the short-cycle delay. ClearControl (RTU-C) is the DDC option on those units. The CoreCommand fault-code table is in the RGED IOM 92-106166-01 and RGEC IOM 92-106691-01 and was not readable via search, so no CoreCommand codes are included; it deserves its own platform entry (e.g. rheem-corecommand).
appliesTo: Rheem/Ruud commercial packaged RK/RL/RQ families, design revision C and later only (RKNL-C, RLNL-C, RKNL-G/H …)

faultCodes.meaning: Controller fault — an error with the RTU-C control board itself ('the only solution is to turn off the power to it and then turn it back on; if the issue persists a new board is necessary').
likelyCauses: RTU-C internal / firmware fault
Power-quality event (brown-out, transient) on the 24 VAC control supply
Corroded or loose connections at the controller board
Failed RTU-C board (47-102883-02/-03 family)
checks: Power the unit off for ~5 minutes and back on; see whether A15 clears (source: JustAnswer thread)
Inspect the controller board connectors for corrosion or loose wiring (source: JustAnswer thread)
Measure 24 VAC at the RTU-C under load and check the control transformer secondary breaker/fuse (field practice)
If A15 returns immediately with clean control power, replace the RTU-C board (source: JustAnswer thread)
faultCodes.source: JustAnswer HVAC thread n7ud2 ('1 lockout, A15 controller fault'); no manufacturer table text seen
faultCodes.notes: Only code confirmed in this session. The full alphanumeric fault table is in the unit IOM (92-23577-80 series for RKNL-B/C) and the Renaissance Technology Guide — transcribe from there before relying on other codes.

faultCodes.meaning: Active unit protection: the RTU-C locks out the compressor circuit when a low pressure trip occurs three times within a thermostat cycle. Spec sheet wording: 'the low-pressure switch shuts off the compressors if low pressure is detected due to loss of charge; built-in Smart Logic reduces nuisance calls by only shutting off compressors after the third detection'.
likelyCauses: Low refrigerant charge / leak
Low evaporator airflow: dirty filters, dirty coil, blower or belt problem, iced coil
Restricted metering device or liquid-line drier
Low-pressure switch, wiring or connector fault (LPS uses a different wire colour and connector size than HPS to prevent cross-wiring)
checks: Read the ALARMS menu on the RTU-C LCD to confirm which circuit tripped (source: 92-103249-01)
Check suction pressure/superheat and charge by subcooling (field practice)
Check airflow: filters, coil, blower amps/belt, and the dirty-filter switch status (field practice)
Verify the LPS closes at the correct pressure and the harness connector is seated (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Rheem 92-103249-01 ClearControl (DDL/DDC) Installation Instructions — active unit protection paragraph ('three times within a thermostat cycle: low pressure trip, high pressure trip, gas heat limit trip'); Rheem spec sheet R11-853 / S11-983 'Pressure/Loss of charge protection' paragraph
faultCodes.notes: Trip-count rule not re-verified: two verification searches found no text containing 'three times within a thermostat cycle' or 'Smart Logic' in 92-103249-01 / R11-853 summaries — confirm in the 92-103249-01 Rev.05 active-protection paragraph before relying on the count.

faultCodes.meaning: Active unit protection: the RTU-C locks out the compressor circuit when a high pressure trip occurs three times within a thermostat cycle.
likelyCauses: Dirty or blocked condenser coil, recirculation of condenser discharge air
Outdoor (condenser) fan not running or wrong rotation
Refrigerant overcharge or non-condensables
Failed high-pressure switch or wiring
checks: Confirm the tripped circuit in the RTU-C ALARMS menu (source: 92-103249-01)
Check head pressure versus ambient, condenser fan operation and coil cleanliness (field practice)
Verify HPS continuity once pressure is below its reset point (field practice)
After correcting the cause, clear the alarm at the display / cycle the thermostat demand to release the lockout (source: 92-103249-01 'find source and clear ALARMS')
faultCodes.source: Rheem 92-103249-01 ClearControl Installation Instructions — active unit protection paragraph ('three times within a thermostat cycle')
faultCodes.notes: Trip-count rule not re-verified: two verification searches found no text containing 'three times within a thermostat cycle' or 'Smart Logic' in 92-103249-01 / R11-853 summaries — confirm in the 92-103249-01 Rev.05 active-protection paragraph before relying on the count.

faultCodes.code: GAS HEAT LIMIT TRIP (active protection lockout)
faultCodes.meaning: Active unit protection: the RTU-C locks out heating when the gas heat limit trips three times within a thermostat cycle. The IFC reports the open limit/rollout to the RTU-C over Modbus ('after a call for heat the IFC checks that the high temperature limit and rollout switches are closed; if either is open, the IFC responds with a fault code').
likelyCauses: Low airflow in heating: dirty filters, dirty evaporator coil, blower/belt problem, high external static, closed dampers
Over-fired heat exchanger (manifold pressure or orifice wrong)
Rollout switch tripped (blocked flue/heat exchanger) — manual reset
Failed limit switch
checks: Check whether a manual-reset rollout switch is open before anything else (field practice)
Measure temperature rise against the nameplate range and external static pressure (field practice)
Verify blower runs at heating speed with correct amps/belt tension (field practice)
Check manifold pressure and clocked gas input (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Rheem 92-103249-01 ClearControl Installation Instructions — active unit protection paragraph and IFC/Modbus heating sequence paragraph
faultCodes.notes: Trip-count rule not re-verified: two verification searches found no text containing 'three times within a thermostat cycle' or 'Smart Logic' in 92-103249-01 / R11-853 summaries — confirm in the 92-103249-01 Rev.05 active-protection paragraph before relying on the count.

faultCodes.code: IFC FAULT — ignition lockout (IFC LED code 1)
faultCodes.meaning: Gas-heat ignition control fault reported to the RTU-C over Modbus: 'the IFC indicates a fault code through MODBUS and the LED flashes a fault code of 1 to indicate lockout is due to failed ignition'.
likelyCauses: No gas / gas valve not opening, low gas pressure
Failed or cracked hot-surface igniter
Dirty or misaligned flame sensor, poor burner ground
Burner/orifice obstruction
checks: Read the IFC LED in the burner compartment: 1 flash = ignition lockout (source: 92-103249-01)
Verify inlet and manifold gas pressure and that the valve opens on trial for ignition (field practice)
Check igniter resistance/glow and flame-sense microamps; clean the sensor (field practice)
Reset by cycling the W demand or unit power after the cause is fixed (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Rheem 92-103249-01 ClearControl Installation Instructions — IFC heating sequence paragraph (IFC board communicates to the RTU-C via MODBUS)

faultCodes.code: IFC FAULT — inducer pressure switch (IFC LED code 2)
faultCodes.meaning: Gas-heat pressure-switch fault reported to the RTU-C over Modbus: 'the IFC checks that both sets of draft inducer pressure switches are open; if either pressure switch set is closed, the IFC will respond with a fault code and flash code 2 on the LED, waiting indefinitely for both sets to open'. Also flashed while the IFC energizes the inducer and waits for the low/high pressure switch to close ('if the high pressure switch does not close within 60 seconds the control flashes 2 and de-energizes the high inducer motor for 5 minutes, then retries').
likelyCauses: Blocked or restricted flue / combustion-air inlet
Condensate backed up into the pressure-switch tubing
Two-stage inducer not reaching high speed, weak inducer motor
Cracked/loose switch tubing, switch stuck closed or open
checks: With the inducer off, confirm both switch sets are open; with it running, measure draft at the switch tap against the setpoint printed on the switch (field practice)
Clear the condensate drain/trap and check the tubing (field practice)
Verify the inducer changes speed on second-stage heat (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Rheem 92-103249-01 ClearControl Installation Instructions — IFC heating sequence paragraphs (code 2 / pressure switches)

faultCodes.meaning: 'The unit mounted fan proving switch monitors the pressure differential across the unit blower to detect when the indoor fan is blowing air. An alarm is sent to the LCD display (and Network if applicable) if the pressure differential indicates that the indoor blower is not operating.'
likelyCauses: Indoor blower not running: motor, contactor/relay, VFD fault, broken belt
Fan proving switch (FPS) tubing disconnected, reversed or plugged
FPS setpoint too high for the unit's operating static
Failed FPS or open wiring to the RTU-C input
checks: Confirm the blower actually runs when commanded (amps, belt, VFD status) (field practice)
Check FPS tubing to the blower section and that the switch closes with the blower running (field practice)
Verify 24 VAC / closure at the RTU-C FPS input with the fan proven (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Rheem spec sheet R11-853 (RKNL-C) / 92-103249-01 — 'Fan Proving Switch' feature description

faultCodes.meaning: 'A pressure differential switch across the return air filters is mounted in the filter section and is connected to the RTU-C control.' The RTU-C 'will signal an increase in static pressure across the air filter, indicating a dirty filter condition' on the display and network. Trip threshold: 'a diagnostic signal is sent to the LCD display if the pressure differential across the filters is at least 0.5 i.w.c.' (92-103249-01).
likelyCauses: Loaded return-air filters
Clogged filter switch (CFS) setpoint too low, tubing reversed or leaking
Blocked return path raising pressure drop across the filter rack
checks: Inspect and replace filters; verify the flex-fit filter rack is fully loaded and seated (field practice)
Check CFS tubing (high side upstream of the filters) and setpoint (field practice)
Verify the switch trips at about 0.5 in. w.c. differential with a manometer across the filter rack (source: 92-103249-01)
faultCodes.source: Rheem spec sheet R11-853 (RKNL-C) 'Clogged Filter Switch' description; 92-103249-01 dirty-filter paragraph

faultCodes.meaning: Smoke detector input (units equipped with supply and/or return smoke detectors): 'The input will shutdown the unit and requires a manual reset.'
likelyCauses: Smoke or dust in the supply/return air stream tripped the detector
Detector not reset after a trip (latched)
Detector sensitivity / dirty sensing chamber, or open wiring at the shutdown input
checks: Check the detector's own trouble/alarm LEDs and reset it at the detector after confirming there is no smoke (field practice)
Verify the shutdown input to the RTU-C is restored (24 VAC / contact closed) after the reset (field practice)
Clean or replace the detector head if it trips with no smoke present (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Rheem 92-103249-01 ClearControl Installation Instructions — smoke detector input description ('only applicable on units equipped with a smoke detector; the input will shutdown the unit and requires a manual reset')

faultCodes.meaning: 'Economizer Faults will trigger a network Alarm and can be read at the unit controller display or remotely through a network connection.' The economizer is controlled by the Economizer Logic Module (ELM) supplied with the economizer; the RTU-C communicates with the ELM for control, setpoints and diagnostics.
likelyCauses: Mixed-air, return-enthalpy, outdoor-enthalpy or CO2 sensor open/shorted
Damper actuator failed, disconnected or not communicating with the ELM
ELM / RTU-C communication wiring fault
checks: Read Economizer Status, mixed air temperature, damper position and CO2 at the RTU-C display (source: R11-853)
Check the ELM's own diagnostics (JADE-type module: see the honeywell-jade-w7220 platform in this pack) and its sensor wiring (field practice)
Drive the damper from the ELM checkout and confirm it moves (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Rheem spec sheet R11-853 (RKNL-C) economizer/ELM paragraphs ('Economizer Faults will trigger a network Alarm...')

faultCodes.meaning: 'The RTU-C control has two inputs to monitor up to two compressor circuits using optional Copeland Comfort Alerts; on dual compressor units only the affected compressor circuit is locked out.' The specific fault is the Comfort Alert flash code (1 long run time, 2 system pressure trip, 3 short cycling, 4 locked rotor, 5 open circuit, 6 open start circuit, 7 open run circuit, 8 welded contactor, 9 low voltage <17 VAC).
likelyCauses: Compressor electrical fault (locked rotor, open winding/circuit, welded contactor)
Repeated pressure-switch trips seen by the module (code 2)
Low control voltage (code 9)
checks: Read the Comfort Alert module's own ALERT LED flash count on the affected circuit; codes are in the compressors pack (coresense-communications-1ph) (field practice)
Check compressor amps/megohms, contactor contacts and 24 VAC control voltage per the flash code (field practice)
Reset by cycling power to the module/unit after the cause is corrected (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Rheem 92-103249-01 ClearControl Installation Instructions — Comfort Alert inputs paragraph; Emerson Comfort Alert user manual 2006ECT-54 (codes 4–9 seen in search summary)

diagnosticTips: Fault/status codes are shown on the controller display in the control compartment; PlusOne Diagnostics ('ClearControl') exposes the same data through the optional DDL/BAS interface (install instructions 92-103249-01).
The IFC (ignition control) on gas units communicates with the RTU-C via Modbus; an ignition fault will appear on the RTU-C display as well as on the IFC LED.
Clearing: most faults clear on power cycle; a lockout that returns immediately points to the safety that caused it (check HPS/LPS, limit, pressure switch history) rather than the board.

Display: the RTU-C has a 16 x 2 character LCD and a five-button keypad on the board in the unit control panel; it 'displays control parameters, diagnostic codes and sensor readings' and the keypad scrolls the menu and makes field-configurable changes (S11-983 / R11-853).

Alarms: scroll to ALARMS on the RTU-C display; the IOM start-up checklist says 'if any ALARMS are present, find source and clear ALARMS'. Alarms are also available over the BAS network (Modbus/BACnet RXRX-AY01/LonWorks) and can be wired to the thermostat 'L' terminal for notification (S11-983).

Clearing: a third-party thread on A15 describes navigating to the current alarms menu and selecting the reset-alarm option; hard faults (controller fault, smoke shutdown) need a power cycle or the device's own manual reset. Diagnostic code information is retained through a power failure (92-103249-01).

RUNTEST: scroll the RTU-C display to RUNTEST mode, choose Heating or Cooling runtest and enter the password to start (92-103249-01 sec. 6.10 Initial Test Sequence); use it to exercise stages without waiting on thermostat demand.

Active protection (as transcribed from 92-103249-01 summaries; the 3-trip count could not be re-verified): low pressure trip, high pressure trip or gas heat limit trip three times within one thermostat cycle locks out that function; on two-compressor units only the affected circuit is locked out. Read which circuit before touching anything.
Gas heat: the IFC talks to the RTU-C over Modbus, so an ignition or pressure-switch fault appears both as an IFC LED flash code (1 = ignition, 2 = pressure switch) and as an RTU-C alarm.

Sensors the RTU-C uses for diagnostics: return air (RAT), discharge/supply air (DAT/SAT), outdoor air (OAT), suction-line freeze sensors (FS, used in place of freezestats), clogged filter switch (CFS) and fan proving switch (FPS). A sensor reading that is obviously wrong on the STATUS screens points to the sensor before the alarm.

controls.name: Rheem/Ruud Integrated Furnace Control (IFC) LED flash codes — standard gas furnace / gas-pack ignition control
controls.description: Single-LED flash-code ignition control used across Rheem and Ruud gas furnaces and gas/electric packaged units (Rheem and Ruud share the platform, so codes are identical). The LED flashes a count, pauses, and repeats. On RKNL-C and later the IFC also reports the fault to the RTU-C via Modbus.

faultCodes.meaning: Pressure switch stuck open — the switch will not close when the inducer is on.
likelyCauses: Blocked or restricted flue/vent or combustion-air inlet
Condensate backed up into the pressure-switch hose (clogged drain/trap)
Inducer motor weak or not running
Cracked/loose pressure-switch tubing, failed pressure switch
checks: With the inducer running, measure draft at the switch tap with a manometer and compare with the switch's setpoint printed on it
Inspect and clear the condensate drain/trap and the switch tubing
Verify inducer runs at full speed and the vent is clear end to end
Jumper the switch only to prove the switch itself (never leave it jumpered)
faultCodes.source: Rheem 'Standard Gas Furnace Flash Codes' (pts.myrheem.com GF_Flash_Code) as summarized by multiple third-party guides (bcwide.ca, burkhardtheating.com, honestfix.com)

faultCodes.meaning: Limit switch open — main limit or roll-out (flame roll-out) control open.
likelyCauses: Low airflow: dirty filter, dirty evaporator coil, blower/belt problem, closed dampers, high external static
Blower not running / failed blower motor or capacitor
Roll-out switch tripped (blocked heat exchanger, flue restriction, burner misalignment) — manual-reset roll-out must be reset
Over-fired unit (gas pressure too high)
checks: Check whether a manual-reset roll-out switch is tripped before anything else
Measure temperature rise against the nameplate range and external static pressure
Verify blower operation in heat (speed/belt/motor amps)
Check manifold gas pressure and clocked input
faultCodes.source: Rheem 'Standard Gas Furnace Flash Codes' as summarized by multiple third-party guides (bcwide.ca, burkhardtheating.com, honestfix.com)

ledPatterns.pattern: Repeating group of N flashes, then pause
ledPatterns.meaning: Fault code N — count the flashes in one group
checks: Compare the count with the flash-code label on the control-box cover / IFC

ledPatterns.pattern: IFC LED — 1 flash (Modbus-linked IFC on RKNL-C+, per 92-103249-01)
ledPatterns.meaning: Lockout due to failed ignition; the same fault is sent to the RTU-C via Modbus and shows as an alarm on the LCD
checks: Check gas supply/manifold pressure, igniter and flame sensor; reset by cycling the heat demand

ledPatterns.pattern: IFC LED — 2 flashes (Modbus-linked IFC on RKNL-C+, per 92-103249-01)
ledPatterns.meaning: Inducer pressure switch fault: a switch set is closed before the inducer starts, or the low/high pressure switch did not close (high switch retried for 60 s every 5 min)
checks: Check draft at the switch tap, tubing, condensate backup and two-speed inducer operation

diagnosticTips: The LED is on the IFC board in the burner/control compartment; the code legend is printed on the board label and the unit's flash-code label (e.g. 92-103343-01 for 2-digit-display furnaces).
A clogged condensate line that backs up into the pressure-switch hose is a common cause of a 2-flash fault on gas packs.
Clear a lockout by cycling thermostat demand (W off/on) or unit power; a roll-out switch is manual reset and must be pressed after the cause is fixed.

controls.name: Honeywell/Resideo JADE W7220 economizer module (Rheem/Ruud factory and field economizers)
controls.description: Two-line LCD economizer controller with alarms shown in the ALARMS menu. Used on Rheem/Ruud commercial packaged units with factory economizers (Rheem economizer literature: RXRD-01MDDAM3 'Vertical Jade', XRD-01RDHAM3) and widely on other brands. Shared table: the W7220 ALARMS table is identical on Carrier EconoMi$er X (factory and CRECOMZR accessory kits), Rheem/Ruud, Lennox, Trane, Daikin/Goodman and other OEM JADE-based economizers — Carrier LLECON-02SI and IIK-CRECOMZR reproduce the same MAT SENS ERR ... DA SENS ALM list. Use this entry for any unit whose economizer board is a W7220. The 17 W7220 alarms here are the full ALARMS list in Honeywell 62-0331/63-2700 (13 base alarms plus DA SENS ERR and the three communicating-actuator alarms); coverage stays 'partial' only because later firmware revisions may add alarms. The JADE W7220 meets Title 24 economizer FDD by way of its sensor and actuator alarms (MAT/OA/RA/DA SENS ERR, ACT ERROR/ACT STALLED, FREEZE ALARM, DA SENS ALM); no source showed separate JADE strings such as 'ECON FAIL', 'DAMPER FAULT', 'EXCESS OA' or 'NOT ECONOMIZING' — those wordings are Title 24 fault categories, not W7220 display text. Belimo ZIP economizer alarms were removed from this platform: no Rheem/Ruud source shows a ZIP fitted to Rheem units. The older W7212/W7213/W7214 EconoMi$er IV logic module (no alarm display) is a separate platform, honeywell-economiser-iv-w7212.

faultCodes.meaning: Indicates that the mixed air sensor has failed or become disconnected. Check the wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists.
likelyCauses: Mixed air (20k NTC C7250 / C7400S) sensor open, shorted or unplugged at the MAT terminals
Broken or chafed sensor lead inside the mixed-air section
Sensor reading outside the controller's valid range (failed thermistor)
checks: Manual: check the wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
Field practice: unplug the sensor and measure resistance; a 20k NTC reads ~20k ohm at 77 F — open or dead-short means a bad sensor or lead
Field practice: MAT is the one sensor the JADE cannot run without — economizer free cooling is unavailable until it clears
faultCodes.source: Honeywell 62-0331 / 63-2700, ALARMS menu table (also ManualsLib 1405190 p.24)

faultCodes.meaning: OA SYLK T ERR / OA SYLK H ERR: Indicates that the outdoor air enthalpy sensor has failed or become disconnected. Check the wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists.
likelyCauses: C7400S outdoor enthalpy (Sylk bus) sensor temperature element failed
S-BUS wiring open, reversed polarity is tolerated but a broken conductor is not
Sensor lost communication after having been detected (device fail)
checks: Manual: check the wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
Manual: the JADE will not alarm a disconnected Sylk device during the 60-minute setup mode after power-up; after that all missing/failed components alarm
Field practice: verify the sensor's DIP/jumper is set to OA (not RA/DA) — a wrong address reads as a missing OA sensor
faultCodes.source: Honeywell 62-0331 / 63-2700, ALARMS menu table

faultCodes.meaning: OA SYLK T ERR / OA SYLK H ERR: Indicates that the outdoor air enthalpy sensor has failed or become disconnected. Check the wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists.
likelyCauses: C7400S outdoor enthalpy sensor humidity element failed
S-BUS wiring problem or sensor disconnected
checks: Manual: check the wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
Field practice: temporarily remove power to the W7220 and restore it once the S-BUS wiring is verified so the module re-detects the sensor
faultCodes.source: Honeywell 62-0331 / 63-2700, ALARMS menu table

faultCodes.meaning: Indicates voltage received by the actuator is below the expected range. (Displayed only when a Sylk-bus communicating actuator is used.)
likelyCauses: Low 24 VAC supply / undersized or overloaded transformer
Voltage drop on long or undersized actuator wiring
Too many Sylk devices on the bus
checks: Field practice: measure 24 VAC at the actuator terminals with the actuator driving; compare to the transformer output
Field practice: check the transformer VA rating against total connected load
faultCodes.source: Honeywell 62-0331 / 63-2700, ALARMS menu table (communicating actuator alarms)

faultCodes.meaning: Indicates that the CO2 sensor has failed, gone out of range, or become disconnected. Check the wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists.
checks: Manual: check the wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
Field practice: measure the sensor output (should be 2-10 Vdc, not 0-10) and the sensor's 24 V supply; verify the DCV configuration matches the sensor type
faultCodes.source: Honeywell 62-0331 / 63-2700, ALARMS menu table
likelyCauses: 2-10 Vdc CO2 sensor output missing or outside range at the CO2 terminals
Sylk-bus TR40 CO2 sensor lost communication
CO2 sensor unpowered or wired to the wrong terminals

faultCodes.meaning: RA SYLK T ERR / RA SYLK H ERR: Indicates that the return air enthalpy sensor has failed or become disconnected. Check the wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists.
checks: Manual: check the wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
Field practice: if a RA sensor was removed on purpose, power-cycle the module so it re-learns the installed devices (setup mode) and stops expecting it
faultCodes.source: Honeywell 62-0331 / 63-2700, ALARMS menu table
likelyCauses: C7400S return-air Sylk sensor temperature element failed or disconnected
Sensor configured for the wrong location (OA/RA/DA setting)

faultCodes.meaning: RA SYLK T ERR / RA SYLK H ERR: Indicates that the return air enthalpy sensor has failed or become disconnected. Check the wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists.
checks: Manual: check the wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
faultCodes.source: Honeywell 62-0331 / 63-2700, ALARMS menu table
likelyCauses: C7400S return-air sensor humidity element failed
S-BUS wiring problem

faultCodes.meaning: Indicates that the discharge air sensor has failed or become disconnected. Check the wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists.
checks: Manual: check the wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
Field practice: the DA sensor is optional — if it was never installed and the alarm appears, the module learned a sensor that has since been removed; power-cycle to re-detect
faultCodes.source: Honeywell 62-0331 / 63-2700, ALARMS menu table
likelyCauses: C7400S discharge-air Sylk sensor failed or disconnected
S-BUS wiring problem

faultCodes.meaning: Indicates that the outdoor air temperature sensor has failed or become disconnected. Check the wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists. (Shown when a 20k hard-wired OA temperature sensor is used; with Sylk sensors the OA SYLK alarms are shown instead.)
checks: Manual: check the wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists
Field practice: measure resistance across the OAT terminals with the sensor disconnected and compare to the 20k NTC table
faultCodes.source: Honeywell 62-0331 / 63-2700, ALARMS menu table
likelyCauses: Hard-wired 20k NTC (C7250) outdoor air temperature sensor open/shorted
Sensor lead damaged in the hood or wiring harness

faultCodes.meaning: Indicates that the actuator has failed or become disconnected. Check for stall, over voltage, under voltage, and actuator count.
checks: Manual: check for stall, over voltage, under voltage, and actuator count
Field practice: run CHECKOUT > damper open/close and watch for ACT STALLED / ACT UNDER V / ACT OVER V, which pinpoint the cause
Field practice: free the damper blades and linkage by hand; verify 24 VAC at the actuator under load
faultCodes.source: Honeywell 62-0331 / 63-2700, ALARMS menu table
likelyCauses: Damper actuator (2-10 Vdc or Sylk MS7505/MS7503) disconnected or failed
Actuator stalled against a bound damper
24 VAC supply to the actuator out of range
More than one Sylk actuator on the bus (actuator count)

faultCodes.meaning: Indicates that the outdoor temperature is below the LOW Temp Lockout setting or the mixed air temperature is below the Lo Setpoint. The alarm will clear when conditions return to normal range.
checks: Manual: alarm clears when conditions return to normal range
Field practice: compare STATUS MAT/OAT readings against a reference thermometer; verify the damper actually drives to minimum when freeze protection is active
Field practice: review MA LO SET and LOW T LOCK in SETPOINTS/ADVANCED SETUP
faultCodes.source: Honeywell 62-0331 / 63-2700, ALARMS menu table; MA LO SET default from SETPOINTS table
likelyCauses: Genuine low outdoor/mixed-air temperature (normal in winter)
MA LO SET (default 45 F, range 35-65 F) set too high for the application
Damper stuck open or minimum position too high, pulling cold air across the MAT sensor
MAT sensor reading low (bad sensor or poor placement)

faultCodes.meaning: Indicates that AUX2 IN is programmed for SHUTDOWN and 24 V has been applied to the AUX 2IN terminal.
checks: Manual: this is a status alarm — the shutdown input is active, not a controller fault
Field practice: measure for 24 VAC at AUX2 IN and trace what is driving it; check the AUX2 IN setting in SYSTEM SETUP
faultCodes.source: Honeywell 62-0331 / 63-2700, ALARMS menu table
likelyCauses: Smoke detector / fire alarm or BAS shutdown relay is energizing AUX2 IN (dampers close)
AUX2 IN mis-programmed as SHUTDOWN when the input is really an occupied/heat input

faultCodes.meaning: Displays if DCV Auto enable has been programmed and the Jade is completing a calibration on the dampers. This alarm will clear once calibration is complete.
checks: Manual: wait — it clears when calibration completes
Field practice: do not judge damper response or run CHECKOUT until the calibration finishes
faultCodes.source: Honeywell 62-0331 / 63-2700, ALARMS menu table
likelyCauses: Normal: DCV CAL ENABLE = AUTO and the module is calibrating damper minimum/max positions after power-up or a setting change

faultCodes.meaning: Indicates that the discharge air temperature is out of the range set in the ADVANCED SETUP Menu (DA LO ALM / DA HI ALM).
checks: Manual: range is set by DA LO ALM (low limit) and DA HI ALM (high limit) in ADVANCED SETUP
Field practice: verify supply air temperature with a probe at the sensor location, then review the alarm limits
faultCodes.source: Honeywell 62-0331 / 63-2700, ALARMS menu table and ADVANCED SETUP table
likelyCauses: Discharge air genuinely too cold or too hot (cooling/heating problem, or economizer over-cooling)
DA LO ALM / DA HI ALM limits set too tight for the equipment
Discharge sensor reading wrong or mounted where it sees stratified air

faultCodes.meaning: Indicates that the discharge air sensor has failed or become disconnected.
likelyCauses: Discharge air sensor open, shorted or disconnected
checks: Check the wiring and replace the sensor if the alarm persists (same treatment as the other SENS ERR alarms)
faultCodes.source: Honeywell 63-2700 / ManualsLib 1405190 W7220 Alarms table

faultCodes.meaning: Indicates voltage received by the actuator is above the expected range. (Displayed only when a Sylk-bus communicating actuator is used.)
likelyCauses: High transformer secondary voltage (wrong primary tap, high line voltage)
Two power sources back-feeding the actuator
checks: Field practice: measure the 24 VAC supply at the actuator; correct the transformer tap or wiring
faultCodes.source: Honeywell 62-0331 / 63-2700, ALARMS menu table (communicating actuator alarms)

faultCodes.meaning: Indicates the actuator stopped before achieving its commanded position. (Displayed only when a Sylk-bus communicating actuator is used.)
likelyCauses: Damper blades bound, iced, or linkage jammed
Actuator stroke/end stops set wrong or damper over-travel
Actuator failed
Field report: an MS7505 gave a stall error during CHECKOUT open/close tests when it was not the only actuator on the W7220's bus
checks: Field practice: run CHECKOUT damper open/close and watch the blades; move the damper by hand with power off to feel for binding
Field practice: confirm only one communicating actuator is connected to the module
faultCodes.source: Honeywell 62-0331 / 63-2700, ALARMS menu table (communicating actuator alarms); HVAC-Talk 2282959 for the multi-actuator field report

diagnosticTips: Display/LEDs: the module is in the economizer/control compartment; use the ▲/▼/Enter/Esc buttons to walk STATUS → SETPOINTS → SYSTEM SETUP → ADVANCED SETUP → CHECKOUT → ALARMS.
CHECKOUT drives the damper open/closed and exercises outputs for testing; STATUS shows live MAT/OAT/RAT, economizer availability and damper position.
Alarms clear automatically when the condition is resolved (e.g. a sensor reconnected); a persistent alarm after wiring is verified means the sensor or actuator is bad.

W7220 display: 2-line, 16-character LCD with four keys (up, down, Enter, Esc) on the module in the unit control box / economizer compartment. Menus: STATUS, SETPOINTS, SYSTEM SETUP, ADVANCED SETUP, CHECKOUT, ALARMS(#). The ALARMS menu title shows the number of active alarms in parentheses; alarms display only while they are active and there is no manual clear — fix the cause and the alarm drops off.
W7220: if one or more alarms are present and there has been no keypad activity for at least 5 minutes, the display automatically shows the ALARMS menu and cycles through the active alarms.

W7220 setup mode: for the first 60 minutes after power-up the module is in setup mode and will not alarm a disconnected OA sensor or Sylk-bus device; after 60 minutes it changes to operation mode and every removed or failed component alarms. Power-cycle the module after removing or replacing Sylk devices so it re-learns the bus.

W7220 CHECKOUT menu drives the damper to min/open/closed, exercises the exhaust, Y1/Y2 and AUX outputs and is the fastest way to reproduce ACT ERROR / ACT STALLED; STATUS shows live MAT, OAT, RAT, DAT, CO2, damper position and ECON AVAIL.

W7220 sensors: hard-wired MAT/OAT are 20k NTC (C7250); Sylk-bus C7400S enthalpy sensors and MS7505/MS7503 Sylk actuators daisy-chain on the S-BUS (polarity-insensitive two-wire). ACT UNDER V / ACT OVER V / ACT STALLED only appear with a communicating actuator.

controls.name: Honeywell W7212 / W7213 / W7214 EconoMi$er IV economizer logic module (pre-Renaissance Rheem/Ruud economizer kits)
controls.description: Potentiometer-set economizer logic module with three status LEDs (Free Cool, DCV, Exhaust) and no alarm display, used on older Rheem/Ruud economizer accessory kits (e.g. ECH-RR25-ENT) fitted to RKNL-A/B, RKKL and RLKL units before the JADE W7220. Diagnose with the resistor checkout table in Honeywell 63-2596.
appliesTo: Rheem/Ruud pre-Renaissance economizer accessory kits (RKNL-A/B, RKKL-B, RLKL-B era)

faultCodes.meaning: The W7212/W7213/W7214 has no alarm display or fault codes; the FREE COOL, DCV and EXHAUST LEDs show operating mode only. Faults are found by the checkout procedure: with 24 VAC applied and the checkout resistors in place, the LEDs and actuator must respond as the 63-2596 checkout table states; a step that does not respond identifies the failed input, sensor or module.
likelyCauses: Enthalpy/dry-bulb sensor (C7400 / C7660) open or out of range
Mixed-air sensor (C7150) open or shorted
Actuator (M7415 / MS7505) not driving
Module failed (no LED response with checkout resistors installed)
checks: Run the 63-2596 checkout: 5.6k ohm across T-T1, 1.2k ohm checkout resistor across SO-+, 620 ohm across SR-+, then step through the LED/actuator table
Verify 24 VAC at TR-TR1 and the actuator drive at P-P1
faultCodes.source: Honeywell 63-2596 W7212/W7213/W7214 Economizer Logic Modules Product Data — LEDs and checkout table

ledPatterns.pattern: W7212/W7213/W7214 EconoMi$er IV: FREE COOL LED on
ledPatterns.meaning: Free cooling is available — outdoor conditions are below the enthalpy/dry-bulb changeover setting and the module will use the damper for first-stage cooling.
checks: Checkout (63-2596): with 24 VAC applied, a 620 ohm resistor across SO and + turns the free cool LED on; removing it turns the LED off
Checkout: with the enthalpy pot set to A the free cool LED turns on and the actuator drives to between 18 and 72 degrees open (5.6k ohm across T-T1 simulates MAT 50-55 F)

ledPatterns.pattern: W7212/W7213/W7214: DCV LED on
ledPatterns.meaning: The module is in demand-control-ventilation mode (CO2 input above the DCV setpoint) and is opening the damper toward DCV MAX.
checks: Checkout: a 9 V battery + to AQ, - to AQ1 turns the DCV and Exhaust LEDs on and drives the actuator to 45 degrees open with DCV MAX at mid position

ledPatterns.pattern: W7212/W7213/W7214: EXHAUST LED on
ledPatterns.meaning: The exhaust fan contact (EXH1/EXH2) is closed — damper position has exceeded the exhaust fan setpoint potentiometer.
checks: Checkout: LED and contacts follow the EXH SET pot; all LEDs off and exhaust contacts open is the starting state of the checkout procedure

ledPatterns.pattern: W7212/W7213/W7214: all LEDs off, damper at minimum
ledPatterns.meaning: No free cooling, no DCV demand and no exhaust call — normal minimum-position ventilation, or the module is unpowered/not seeing a fan call.
checks: Checkout preparation (63-2596): disconnect power at TR/TR1, disconnect devices at P and P1 and jumper P to P1, 5.6k ohm across T and T1, jumper TR to 1 (W7212: also TR to N), 1.2k ohm 4074EJM checkout resistor across SO and +, 620 ohm across SR and +, MIN POS and DCV MAX fully CCW, then apply 24 VAC to TR/TR1 and step through the table

diagnosticTips: W7212/W7213/W7214 EconoMi$er IV has no alarm display — only the three LEDs (Free Cool, DCV, Exhaust) and potentiometers; diagnose with the resistor checkout table in Honeywell 63-2596 (5.6k across T-T1, 1.2k checkout resistor across SO-+, 620 ohm across SR-+).
